LESSON: WRITING 9.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITIONS (240-280 WORDS)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.5: Writing 9.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (240-280 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (240-280 words), part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why do we enjoy reading stories? 2. How can you make your composition interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recall a specific event, emotion or experience that affected them greatly.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (240-280 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. plan a narrative composition using prewriting techniques • Identify the parts of narrative composition. • Work with peers to narrate events, feelings or experiences that impacted them. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by the teacher or peers. Allow more time for learners 1. Why do we enjoy reading stories? 2. How can you make your composition interesting? 84

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (240-280 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create a narrative composition using revealing details

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (240-280 words) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the value of quality narrative compositions with speech difficulties as they present their views. • Work with peers to plan a narrative composition, • Write a narrative composition individually. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to write. • Collaborate with peers to check each other’s work for: - Correctness of language - Relevance to the topic - Punctuation - Spelling • Review their work individually and make corrections where necessary, • Publish their work by either: - Sharing it through email - Sharing it through social media - Pasting the work on posters - Posting the work in class and conducting a gallery walk. 3. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions (240-280 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination – making observations enhances the learner’s creativity as they create narrative compositions on

a variety of topics.

• Digital literacy – interacting with digital technology is enhanced as the learner shares their work via email and on social

media.

Values:
Unity is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to revise and make their work better.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social cohesion: Working with peers while conducting the gallery walk makes learners learn to live harmoniously.

Link to other subjects:

The concept of narrative composition writing is related to the concept types of writing in both Kiswahili and creative Arts.
